notes: A CORRECTION, NOT A NEW ADJUDICATION. bmdb 1553 (library-ruling consistency pass), sqlite, b7: the ADR-0010 build-configuration sub-pass. EXPORT SURFACE: libsqlite3 is built and installed (main.mk:1599-1608, install-lib/install-dll), and ext/ sources are compiled into it or built as documented loadable extensions (ext/misc/README.md); SQLITE_PRIVATE makes internal functions static only in the amalgamation build, and the separate-source build also compiles (ADR-0010). Every non-static function in these sources therefore has an open caller set (ADR-0011 742a1571, 6b28c8d7), and in-tree call sites prove nothing about a value arriving through its parameters. SELECTION: existing FP labels on non-static functions in exported sources whose recorded reason is caller-side (callers, call sites, contract, precondition, "always valid/never NULL"); tool-only files with their own main() excluded. METHOD: each row read at source by a reviewer; FP -> TP only where the verdict rested solely on callers for a parameter-derived value. Rows with a real in-function basis (a guard present in every build, a null-tolerant callee, a misfire, a value not from a parameter, a language guarantee) or where the keyword match was noise keep FP. assert/DEBUGASSERT/NEVER()/ALWAYS() are not guards (each compiles out or constant-folds in a compilable build). A fresh-context refuter re-checked a random sample of flips and stands. RESULT: 256 rows reviewed, 79 flip FP -> TP here, 177 keep FP. SUB-PASS: FP labels whose recorded reason rests on build configuration (NEVER()/ALWAYS() guards, which are (0)/(1) under SQLITE_OMIT_AUXILIARY_SAFETY_CHECKS, sqliteInt.h:534-536; asserts stripped under NDEBUG; code live only under SQLITE_DEBUG/SQLITE_TEST; "default build" readings). Under ADR-0010 every compilable configuration counts, so these flip where the construct is live and unproven in some compilable build; labels in files outside the declared scope are not touched. Counting basis: distinct (project, commit, file, line, rule) keys. No precision claim is made here.
